newsitem.title: USA: USDA - 96/97 world centrifugal sugar crop 124 MMT.
newsitem.headline: USDA - 96/97 world centrifugal sugar crop 124 MMT.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Department Wednesday revised down its estimate for 1996/97 world centrifugal sugar production to 124.0 million tonnes from 125.0 million tonnes forecast in November.
In its monthly World Agricultural Production report, USDA said the 1996/97 world sugar output estimate remained above 122.5 million tonnes crop seen in 1995/96.

It said the 1996/97 estimate for India, the world's largest sugar producer, was 15.6 million tonnes, down eight percent from the November forecast of 17.0 million tonnes and off 15 percent from last season's record outturn of 18.3 million tonnes.

USDA said partially offsetting the sharp decline in India, the forecast for 1996/97 European Union sugar production was raised by three percent to 17.7 million tonnes from 17.2 million tonnes forecast in November, and was four percent higher than 17.0 million tonnes last season.

Sugar output in Brazil was revised up to an all-time high of 14.7 million tonnes from 14.5 million tonnes estimated in November and was seven percent above the previous record of 13.7 million tonnes last season.
The forecast for Cuba's 1996/97 sugar crop was unchanged at 4.6 million tonnes versus 4.45 million tonnes last season.

USDA said other major-producing countries with upward revisions in 1996/97 sugar production since the November forecast included Poland, up 246,000 tonnes to 2.4 million tonnes; the United States, up 95,000 tonnes to 6.6 million tonnes; and Mexico, up 100,000 tonnes to 4.7 million tonnes.
USDA said among the major producing countries with downward revisions, the forecasts for Thailand and Pakistan dipped by 200,000 tonnes to 6.3 million and 2.6 million respectively.
USDA also lowered its forecast for Russia sugar output by 150,000 tonnes to 1.75 million tonnes and pegged the Ukraine sugar crop at 2.9 million tonnes, down 100,000 from the November estimate.
South Africa's 1996/97 sugar crop was estimated at 2.6 million tonnes, down 100,000 from the November forecast.
